classification.difficultyReason: Use the supplied proof scaffolds to establish a parallelogram, select SAS or SSS from explicit givens, and conclude equal sides or supplementary equal angles.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Prove that: If a parallelogram has two adjacent sides equal, then the parallelogram is a rhombus.

spec.description: Parallelogram ABCD with matching single ticks on AB and BC, single parallel arrows on AD and BC, and double parallel arrows on AB and DC. Ordinary source blue is rendered black.
spec.mathematics: AB parallel DC; AD parallel BC; AB equals BC.
spec.answerVisibility: All givens visible; no solution annotations.

answer.worked: $AB=CD$ and $BC=AD$ because opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal. Also $AB=BC$ is given. Hence $AB=BC=CD=DA$, so all four sides are equal and $ABCD$ is a rhombus.

children.label: b
children.prompt:
Prove that: If the diagonals of a quadrilateral bisect each other at right angles, then the quadrilateral is a rhombus.

The diagonals of the quadrilateral $ASBT$ meet at right angles at $M$ and bisect each other.

spec.description: ASBT has crossing diagonals AB and TS at M; AM and MB have double ticks, TM and MS single ticks, and the AMS sector has a right-angle square.

answer.worked: The diagonals of $ASBT$ bisect each other. By the diagonal test for a parallelogram, $ASBT$ is a parallelogram.
$SM=TM$ (given), $\angle AMS=\angle AMT=90^\circ$ (the diagonals meet at right angles), and $AM=AM$ (common side). Therefore $\triangle AMS\equiv\triangle AMT$ by SAS.

children.label: iii
children.prompt: Hence prove that $AS=AT$; that is, $ASBT$ is a rhombus.

answer.short: $AS=AT$ (matching sides of congruent triangles). Thus $ASBT$ is a rhombus.
answer.worked: $AS=AT$ because they are matching sides of the congruent triangles $AMS$ and $AMT$. Since $ASBT$ is a parallelogram, its opposite sides are equal: $AS=BT$ and $AT=SB$. Hence all four sides are equal, so $ASBT$ is a rhombus.

children.label: c
children.prompt:
Prove that: If the diagonals of a quadrilateral have equal length and bisect each other, then the quadrilateral is a rectangle.

The diagonals of the quadrilateral $RSTU$ have equal length and bisect each other.

spec.description: RSTU with both diagonals drawn and four matching double ticks, one on each diagonal half. The crossing is unlabelled. No right-angle markers are supplied.
spec.mathematics: RT=US and each diagonal bisects the other; all four half-diagonals are equal.
spec.answerVisibility: Given diagonal markings only; no inferred right angles shown.

answer.worked: The diagonals of $RSTU$ bisect each other. By the diagonal test for a parallelogram, $RSTU$ is a parallelogram.
$US=RT$ (given), $RS=SR$ (common side), and $RU=ST$ (opposite sides of parallelogram $RSTU$). Therefore $\triangle URS\equiv\triangle TSR$ by SSS.

answer.short: $\angle URS=\angle TSR$ (matching angles of congruent triangles).
answer.worked: Since $\triangle URS\equiv\triangle TSR$, their matching angles are equal. Hence $\angle URS=\angle TSR$.

answer.short:
$\angle URS=90^\circ$.

The equal co-interior angles sum to $180^\circ$.
answer.worked:
Since $UR\parallel ST$, the co-interior angles satisfy
$$\begin{align*}\angle URS+\angle TSR&=180^\circ\\2\angle URS&=180^\circ\\\angle URS&=90^\circ.\end{align*}$$
The opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal, so $\angle UTS=90^\circ$. Each remaining angle is supplementary to $\angle URS$, so both are also $90^\circ$. Thus $RSTU$ is a rectangle.
